claims.text: Womb Watch is an observational feasibility study of a smartphone app for assessing fetal movements.
claims.quote:
Feasibility Trial of the Womb Watch Smartphone App To Assess Fetal Movements
This trial is a prospective, observational, feasibility study of 60 patients that includes both low-risk and high-risk pregnant women to examine the usability of the Womb Watch smartphone application.
claims.limitations: Purpose, not established efficacy. Conflicting enrollment counts excluded from film.

claims.text: The registry lists recruiting sites in Austin, Galveston and Houston, Texas.
claims.limitations: Exact JSON values; registry-reported status, not on-site confirmation.

claims.text: Participants are asked to record for 15 minutes daily using a smartphone microphone placed against the pregnant abdomen.
claims.quote: Pregnant women between 28 - 40 weeks gestation will audio daily for 15 minutes using their personal smartphone with upload to the Womb Watch app. The microphone of the smartphone will be placed against the pregnant uterus.
claims.limitations: Study procedure, not advice to viewers.

claims.text: The study uses AI to analyze recordings for gross body movements, fetal breathing and fetal hiccups.
claims.quote: Pregnant women between 28 - 40 weeks gestation will audio daily for 15 minutes using their personal smartphone with upload to the Womb Watch app. The microphone of the smartphone will be placed against the pregnant uterus. The audio files will be uploaded from the Womb Watch app via Google Firestore to an encrypted database at the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC-UT Austin). After the audio recording is uploaded, participants will be asked to assess the strength of fetal movements using a Likert scale in the app. Artificial intelligence will be employed to determine the number and strength of three categories of fetal movements: gross body movements, fetal breathing and fetal hiccups. Participants will receive the AI analysis regarding these movements through the customized app.
claims.limitations: Intended analysis, not established detection reliability or diagnosis.

claims.text: The protocol explicitly describes app results as experimental and not diagnostic.
claims.quote: It will be emphasized that any results from the Womb Watch app are experimental and are not diagnostic.

claims.text: The app records all audible sounds; noisy recordings can be deleted and repeated.
claims.quote: All participants will utilize the Womb Watch smartphone application from enrollment until delivery. Participants will be asked to use Womb Watch for 15 minutes daily, preferably in the evening at a time of their choosing. Participants will be informed during consent that the smartphone will record more than just the fetal movement sounds, and as such they should record in a quiet space with minimal conversations. In addition to the intended recording of sounds produced by fetal movement, the app will record all audible sounds. Participants will be informed that audio files which are transmitted to TACC for analysis will be deidentified and the sounds recorded will not be traceable back to them-only the frequency of sound associated with fetal movement sounds will be analyzed. In situations where an audio recording is complicated by noise disruptions in the environment, participants will have the option to delete the recording and re-record a new audio file. The app is designed such that no more than one audio file will be on their phone at a given time.
claims.limitations: No promise that only fetal movement is captured.

claims.text: The feasibility trial compares smartphone brands, models and cases and gathers participant feedback.
claims.quote:
Audio signals from different models and brands of smartphones with or without smartphone cases will be compared in our AI model.

Participants using the pilot Womb Watch smartphone application will receive feedback on fetal movement assessment and help researchers determine if the application needs to be modified for real-world use.

claims.text: The current study reviews routine ultrasound records for amniotic fluid levels that may affect audio/model.
claims.quote:
Participant ultrasound records will be reviewed for the duration of their study timeline. We will record their amniotic fluid index (AFI). We believe this may affect the audio quality of fetal movement assessment.
From the time of enrollment at 28 to 32 weeks' gestation, up until delivery. AFI will be assessed only after a participant has an ultrasound as part of their routine pregnancy care.
claims.limitations: Not simultaneous validation of each recording.

claims.text: An earlier pilot compared audio assessments with movements recorded during simultaneous ultrasound.
claims.quote: In our recent pilot STUDY00001552 of 205 pregnant patients, placement of the iPhone10 microphone directly on the maternal abdominal wall was utilized to detect fetal movements. AI assessment of the audio recordings proved superior to maternal perception of fetal movements that were recorded during simultaneous ultrasound (gross fetal movements: 64% audio vs 18% maternal; breathing: 93% vs 3%, hiccups: 73% vs 3%).
claims.limitations: Background only. Prior sample size differs between sources; omit percentages and sample size from film. Does not prove current clinical performance.

claims.text: The registry reports recruiting, verified in September 2026, with its last update posted September 14, 2026.
claims.limitations: September 14 is posting date, not launch. Actual start is August 6, 2026.

claims.text: The protocol anticipates no direct benefit to participants.
claims.quote: ☒ There is no anticipated direct benefit to participants.

claims.text: The investigator-developed AI model is hosted by UT TACC.
claims.quote: The model is investigator-developed by Co-I, Dr. Kelly Gaither and internally hosted by UT TACC. A deep learning/machine learning model will be employed to determine the number of three categories of fetal movements based on these files: gross body movements, fetal breathing and fetal hiccups.
claims.limitations: The preceding paragraph expands TACC as Texas Advanced Computing Center.

claims.limitations: Exact quote joins sentence across page break; source example, not observed field use.

claims.text: The protocol shows a prototype trends screen and requires an experimental-only, non-diagnostic disclaimer.
claims.quote: Within the application, participants will be able to view their trends, to include fetal movement, fetal breathing, fetal hiccups and the intensity scores they’ve completed using a Likert scale. A disclaimer will notify participants that the values/trends are not diagnostic, that the app is experimental only.
claims.limitations: Prototype plotted values are not current study results.

claims.text: The protocol specifies holding the smartphone vertically against the pregnant abdomen to register audio.
claims.quote: Audio signals will be registered by the participant using the microphone of the smartphone held vertically against the pregnant uterus.
claims.limitations: Study procedure; conceptual images must not impersonate observed use.

claims.text: Researchers track participant anxiety using surveys while testing daily app use.
claims.quote: Participants will complete GAD-7 surveys at the time of enrollment, once every 4 weeks throughout pregnancy and one final GAD-7 survey after delivery. This is to ensure that the app is not creating anxiety in participants. If a participant scores 10+ on any of the GAD-7 surveys, they may be withdrawn from the study and referred for appropriate follow up.
claims.limitations: Monitoring anxiety is a study safeguard/outcome, not proof of reassurance or improved wellbeing.

claims.text: The prototype app Instructions screen explicitly says it is not intended to determine decreased fetal movements.
claims.quote: This app is NOT intended to determine if your baby has decreased fetal movements.

rejected.claim: Proven reliable monitoring, diagnosis, stillbirth prevention, or replacement for clinical care.
rejected.reason: No current results posted; protocol says experimental/non-diagnostic and no anticipated direct benefit. Prevention is an eventual goal.

rejected.claim: Current at-home recordings are individually validated against simultaneous ultrasound.
rejected.reason: Simultaneous ultrasound describes earlier STUDY00001552 only; current study uses routine ultrasound records for amniotic fluid.

rejected.claim: A single consistent current enrollment total.
rejected.reason: July 31 protocol says 75 total, 25 per site; September 14 registry says estimated 60 total, 20 per site. Omit film total; retain discrepancy.

rejected.claim: A single undisputed prior pilot sample size.
rejected.reason: Protocol says 200, registry 205. No reconciliation. Exclude prior sample size and efficacy statistics from film.

rejected.claim: A consistent specific extra phone sensor inventory.
rejected.reason: Protocol names gyroscope and accelerometer; registry names gyroscope and ambient light sensor. Omit inventory.
That is registry update posting. Actual study start is August 6, 2026.

rejected.claim: Only fetal sounds are recorded or the example trace proves fetal health.
rejected.reason: All audible sounds are recorded. Prototype screen values are examples, not results or diagnosis.

rejected.claim: Womb Watch is a fetal heartbeat monitor.
rejected.reason: Sources describe movement, breathing movements and hiccups, not substitution for fetal heart-rate monitoring.

limitations: Both documents are investigator/sponsor-provided primary evidence, not independent efficacy corroboration.
